To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have performed a search for extremely high energy neutrinos using data taken with the half completed IceCube detector.
the analysis of a 333.5 day sample of data from the IceCube detector, taken from April 2008 to May 2009, with the half-completion of IceCube, has yielded no signal candidates.

(a) the IceCube detector has been used to set a new limit on the diffuse neutrino flux from the entire sky, and (b) no significant excess of events was found, which allows us to set limits on the neutrino flux from a number of potential sources.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for neutrinos of cosmic origin in the energy range above 10(6)-10(7) GeV.
the search for neutrinos with energies above the TeV threshold.
the search for high-energy neutrinos in the energy range from 10(6)-10(9)GeV with the partially completed IceCube neutrino telescope in the South Pole.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no evidence for the presence of an E-2 neutrino spectrum has been found in this energy region.
no significant excess of events was found in the IceCube data, and the most likely explanation of this is a null result.

the IceCube 22 string array has been able to place an upper limit on the flux of cosmic neutrino of E-2 spectrum at a level of 3.6 X 10(-8), for energies ranging from 2 X 10(6 )to 6.3 X 10(9), which is a factor of 10 below the flux expected from the Waxman-Bahcall bound.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have set a model-independent limit on the flux of cosmic neutrino with an E-(-2) spectrum in the energy region of 2 x 10(7)-6.3 x (10)(9) GeV.
we have set a model-independent limit on the flux of cosmic neutrino at the highest energies, and we have also set a limit on the flux with an E- 2 spectrum.

the IceCube detector is now sensitive to the fluxes expected in many models.
IceCube has set the most stringent limit to date on the E-2 neutrino flux from all sources, and the most stringent limit on the E-3 flux from all sources in the energy range from 10(6)-10(9)GeV.
